title: Multi-Agent Delegation Expands Permission Scope

invariant.statement: When agent A delegates a task to agent B, the effective permissions for the delegated call must be the intersection of A's and B's permissions, never B's permissions alone.

claim.statement: If a delegated call from agent A to agent B authorizes against B's own permission set rather than the intersection of A's and B's, then any user who can prompt A can leverage A as a stepping stone to invoke any tool B has — even tools A is not authorized to call directly. This is privilege escalation by delegation.

mitigation.summary: Every delegation passes a capability token bound to the caller's permissions. The callee's dispatcher computes effective_permissions = caller_permissions ∩ callee_permissions for the delegated call. Tokens are short-lived, signed, and bound to a specific tool name. Without a valid token, the callee refuses the delegation.

references: OWASP LLM07: Insecure Plugin Design (delegation variant)
